data.name: Bug Attack!
data.detailed_description:
Bug Attack! is a game inspired by arcade classics including Missile Command and Space Invaders.

Players are tasked with protecting their building as long as they can. Bugs emerge from the ground, many of which from random locations, at an increasing rate. Which is the greater enemy? The bug horde, or your own nerves?

To help, once you've earned certain amounts of points, you earn powerful bug bombs, and health-restoring building repair kits- but not even these can fight the bugs off for long!


Want to team up with a friend? Plug in a controller, and a second player can take command of a building-mounted turret(don't ask, it's a game!) to help fight off the never ending waves of creepy crawlies.


Tired of Bugs? Try to protect your wallet from the relentless savings! This mode is for one or two players, and replicates with 100% accuracy the pain your wallet feels when those Sales hit and light up your wishlist.


The Steam Version of Bug Attack! includes extras and achievements, which you unlock by scoring points over time. These unlock a variety of fun bonus options and extra gameplay modes!

Bug Attack! will continue to be supported post-launch with new modes, functionality, and extra content, free of charge.

reviews.review:
Bug Attack! is a deliberately straightforward arcade experience that embraces the philosophy of classic score-chasing games rather than attempting to bury its premise beneath complicated systems. Developed by David Vogt and The Ludicrous Ones and published by DLV Games, the game revolves around defending a building from an infestation that becomes progressively more difficult to contain. Its influences from older arcade titles are easy to recognize, particularly in the emphasis on immediate action, survival, rapidly escalating pressure, and the constant temptation to attempt one more run for a better score. It is a modest production by design, but its simplicity gives it an accessible quality that suits short gaming sessions.

The basic objective is immediately understandable. Bugs emerge from the ground at unpredictable positions and threaten the structure under the player's protection. Eliminating them initially feels manageable, but the rate at which enemies appear continues to increase. Eventually, the player has to divide attention between numerous threats while reacting quickly enough to prevent excessive damage. There is no expectation that the assault can be permanently stopped; survival becomes a matter of delaying the inevitable for as long as possible. This gives the score genuine importance because improvement can be measured directly through longer survival and more effective defensive play.

The experience gains a little more tactical depth through rewards earned after reaching certain scoring milestones. Bug bombs can provide valuable assistance when the infestation becomes overwhelming, while repair kits allow damage to the building to be recovered. Neither resource eliminates the underlying challenge, so deciding when to use these advantages matters. Spending an emergency tool too early can leave the player vulnerable later, whereas waiting too long risks allowing the situation to collapse before the item becomes useful. These mechanics are simple, but they prevent the action from becoming entirely dependent on reflexes.

Multiplayer is one of the more appealing extensions of the concept. A second player can participate locally and operate a turret positioned on the building, transforming the frantic defense into a cooperative exercise. Dividing responsibilities between two people gives the game a different rhythm and can make the increasingly crowded encounters more entertaining. Shared-screen competitive functionality is also supported, along with Remote Play Together. These options are particularly appropriate for an arcade game where individual rounds can be enjoyed without requiring players to commit to an elaborate campaign or progression system.

Bug Attack! also contains a humorous alternative mode in which the objective involves protecting a wallet from relentless savings and sales. It is an intentionally playful variation on the main premise and provides some welcome personality beyond the insect-defense scenario. Accumulating points can unlock additional content, modes, bonuses, and other extras, while Steam achievements provide secondary objectives for completion-minded players. None of these additions radically changes the core experience, but they give repeated sessions a little more purpose than simply restarting the same survival challenge indefinitely.

Visually, the game favors a retro 2D pixel presentation that complements its arcade structure. It does not depend on elaborate graphics or cinematic spectacle, and that restraint works reasonably well because readability is considerably more important when enemies begin appearing rapidly. The old-school presentation also reinforces the feeling that this is intended as a modern interpretation of an earlier generation of arcade design. The atmosphere remains lighthearted even as the difficulty rises, preventing the increasingly frantic action from becoming unnecessarily serious.

Repetition is inevitably the largest weakness. The central mechanic remains focused on defending an objective from an escalating stream of enemies, meaning players who require extensive campaigns, narrative progression, exploration, character development, or constantly changing mechanics may lose interest relatively quickly. The longevity instead comes from personal improvement. Someone who enjoys beating a previous high score, surviving another wave, mastering resource timing, or competing alongside another player will find substantially more replay value. It is therefore best treated as a compact arcade diversion rather than a large-scale action game.

The game also benefits from being accessible without requiring a conventional purchase of the main experience. An optional Supporter's Pack exists for players who want additional material or wish to support the project, but the fundamental game can be approached without that commitment. This makes experimenting with its particular brand of retro score chasing considerably easier and suits the deliberately uncomplicated nature of the overall package.

For Steam Deck users, Bug Attack! does not currently carry an official Steam Deck Verified or Playable designation, so compatibility should be considered unverified rather than guaranteed. The game is designed for Windows and offers partial controller support. Its lightweight 2D presentation and controller functionality suggest that it may be a reasonable candidate for running through SteamOS compatibility technology, but those characteristics should not be interpreted as confirmation of flawless operation. Players specifically purchasing or installing it for handheld use should therefore expect that adjustments or compatibility limitations may be possible.

Bug Attack! ultimately understands the appeal of traditional arcade gaming: simple rules, rapidly increasing difficulty, immediate restarts, and the pursuit of a better performance. Its resource mechanics, cooperative possibilities, humorous alternate content, unlockables, and achievements add useful variety without complicating the foundation. It will not satisfy players searching for deep progression or a lengthy campaign, but as an accessible retro-inspired survival challenge, it delivers an enjoyable and appropriately focused experience.

Rating: 7/10
